 THIS MFA AND MFA.CROB ARE, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Miscellaneous First Appeal No.5926/2017 is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-Insurance Company,
challenging the judgment and award dated 14.12.2016, passed in NC: 2024:KHC:21251 M.V.C.
No.960/2015, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Channarayapatna, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) questioning the quantum of compensation.
2. MFA Crob No.131/2019 is filed under Order 41 Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the claimant seeking for enhancement of compensation.
Brief facts:
3. Smt. Shantamma was traveling in an autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02-3322 on B.M. Road near Gullenahalli Byepass road, at that time, driver of Scorpio Car bearing Reg.No.TN-07-BA-9453 driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the autorickshaw and the inmate suffered severe injuries.

Hence, a claim petition was filed by the petitioner i.e, husband of the deceased under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the death of his wife in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded a compensation of a sum of Rs.11,82,438/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit, under various heads as follows :-
1. Funeral Expenses Rs. 25,000/-

The Tribunal held respondent No.2/Insurance Company therein, to pay the compensation.

5. Heard arguments of learned counsel for both the parties and perused the materials on record.
NC: 2024:KHC:21251 6.
The accident in question and the fact of death of Smt. Shantamma, wife of the petitioner/claimant in the road traffic accident are not in dispute.
The deceased was aged 40 years at the time of accident and was working as a Tailor.
But no evidence is produced to prove the income of the deceased.

Therefore, considering the accident being of the year 2015, notional income of Rs.9,000/-
per month is taken into consideration.
Forty percent of the monthly income is added towards loss of future prospects in life.
Husband is the claimant, hence 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses.
The proper multiplier adopted is '15'.
As per Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded under the head NC: 2024:KHC:21251 'loss of consortium'.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.4,000/- is added,
hence Rs.44,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium'.
8.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,13,688/- towards 'Medical Expenses', which is as per the medical bills and receipts produced and hence kept in tact.
9. Towards Funeral expenses a sum of Rs.15,000 + 1,500 (10%) = Rs.16,500/- is awarded.

10. Towards Loss of Estate a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded and 10% is added towards escalation,
hence a sum of Rs.16,500/- is awarded as against Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for a total enhanced compensation, under various heads as follows:
a. Loss of dependency : Rs.15,12,000/-
b.

Medical Expenses : Rs. 1,13,688/-
c. Loss of consortium : Rs. 44,000/-
 d. Loss of estate : Rs. 16,500/-
 e.
Therefore, the appellant is awarded a total compensation of Rs.17,02,688/- as against the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.11,82,438/-.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.5,20,250/- (Rs.17,02,688/- less Rs.11,82,438/-), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The rate of interest is reduced from 9% to 6%.

11. Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:21251 ORDER i.
The Appeal filed by the Insurance Company and and MFA Crob filed by claimant are allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 14.12.2016, passed in MVC No.960/2015, on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Channarayapatna, is modified to an extent that the appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.5,20,250/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Twenty Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Only), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The rate of interest is reduced from 9% to 6%.
iv. The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
